recommendation.summary: S5 FD-passing handoff with a state transformer (in-memory state schema changed).
justification: the layout of in-memory state changed, so no in-process mechanism can keep the old objects; the new process needs the old state mapped to the new schema (Kitsune/MCR-style state transfer)
a transformer skeleton was generated (old -> new, field by field, TODOs for added/retyped fields)

S6 blockers (3): github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.Compressor.Handler: closures created before the patch (e.g. middleware chains built at start-up) keep the old code; only newly created closures see the fix; github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.compressResponseWriter: layout of in-memory state type changed; github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.compressResponseWriter: layout of in-memory state type changed
alternatives: rolling update if losing the in-memory state is acceptable (cold caches)
risks: changed functions are small enough to be inlined; with S6 slot trampolines the call still dispatches through the slot, but raw binary patching (internal/livepatch) must also patch the inlining callers: github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.compressResponseWriter.Close, github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.compressResponseWriter.Flush, github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.compressResponseWriter.Hijack, github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.compressResponseWriter.Push, github.com/go-chi/chi/v5/middleware.compressResponseWriter.Write
no patched function has a context.Context parameter: S6 gives per-call (not per-request) consistency, so one request may mix old and new versions of the 4 functions
state transformer must be completed and reviewed; encoding/json does not carry unexported fields, so the S5 state envelope needs an explicit DTO for them
